items.title: bug(desktop): "Preview unavailable / Invalid preview URL" when clicking artifact toast message
items.body:
## Bug Description

When the agent produces a file artifact (e.g. a PDF via `write_file` or `weasyprint`), a toast notification appears above the chat window showing the file path. Clicking the toast to preview/open the artifact produces an error:

> Preview unavailable
> Invalid preview URL

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Hermes Desktop session on a remote box (agent running on a remote Linux host, desktop UI connected remotely)
2. Have the agent generate a file artifact (e.g. `weasyprint output.html /home/agent/report.pdf`)
3. The agent delivers the file via `MEDIA:/home/agent/report.pdf`
4. A toast notification appears above the chat window with the file path
5. Click the toast

## Expected Behavior

The file should open in a preview pane or download to the local machine.

## Actual Behavior

Error message displayed: "Preview unavailable / Invalid preview URL"

The file is accessible via the `MEDIA:` link in the chat message itself (which works correctly), but the toast notification click handler appears to construct a different URL that fails.

## Likely Cause

The toast click handler likely constructs a preview URL from the absolute file path on the remote host (e.g. `file:///home/agent/report.pdf`), which is not a valid URL from the desktop client perspective when the agent runs on a remote box. The `MEDIA:` delivery in the chat message works because it goes through a different code path (likely the artifact delivery mechanism), but the toast notification seems to use a separate URL construction that does not account for remote agent setups.

## Environment

- Agent: running on remote Linux host (Ubuntu 22.04)
- Desktop: connected remotely (not localhost)
- Connection: Tailscale
- File path: `/home/agent/Data-Center-Report-Littleton-NH.pdf`
- Artifact type: PDF generated via `weasyprint`

## Additional Context

The `MEDIA:` link in the chat message body works correctly and the file is accessible that way. The issue is specifically with the toast notification click handler.

items.body:
### Summary

When a user sends a photo **while the agent is mid-turn** (executing tools), the image is downloaded and cached to disk but is never injected into the running turn. The agent reports "no image received / your message was text only," even though the file exists in the image cache. Text messages that arrive mid-turn are correctly steered into the turn; images are not.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `busy_input_mode: steer` (Telegram platform).
2. Send the agent a request that triggers a long, multi-tool turn.
3. While that turn is running, send a photo (with or without a caption).
4. After the turn completes, ask the agent about the screenshot.

**Expected:** the agent sees the image (steered into the current turn, or picked up on the next turn).
**Actual:** the agent says it received no image; the file is present in the image cache but absent from the conversation context.

### Root cause (from source)

Inbound photos are handled by a separate batching path in `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` (`_pending_photo_batches` / `_flush_photo_batch`, gated by `HERMES_TELEGRAM_MEDIA_BATCH_DELAY_SECONDS`). This path emits a media `MessageEvent` but has no integration with the `steer` / busy-input mechanism in `gateway/run.py` — which exists for text but not for media. As a result, a photo event emitted while the agent is busy is neither steered into the in-flight turn nor reliably queued to the next one, so it is dropped from context while still being cached to disk.

### Impact

Any image sent while the agent is working is silently lost from the conversation. The user believes the agent ignored their screenshot, when in fact it never entered the model's context.

### Suggested fix

Route media `MessageEvent`s through the same steer/queue path as text so they are appended to the current turn's context (or queued to the next turn) rather than dropped.

### Environment

- hermes-agent 0.18.0
- Telegram platform
- `busy_input_mode: steer`

items.title: [Bug]: > Hermes Desktop “Check for updates” checks the remote container instead of the Desktop app**
items.body:
### Bug Description

When Hermes Desktop is connected to a remote Nous-hosted cloud agent, invoking the Desktop app’s generic **Check for updates** control does not check whether the locally installed Desktop application can be updated. It instead checks the connected remote backend and displays the backend’s container-management restriction as though it applied to the Desktop app:

```text
Update not available
Hermes updates are managed outside this dashboard in containerized environments.
```

That response is accurate for the managed cloud backend, but misleading in a native Desktop window. The user was trying to update the Desktop client installed on their own computer, not the remote container.

This leaves the Desktop app’s update status or update method unclear whenever it is in remote mode, and conflates two independently versioned installations:

1. the local Electron Desktop client; and
2. the remote Hermes backend.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install and open Hermes Desktop.
2. Configure **Settings → Gateway → Remote gateway** and connect successfully to a managed/containerized Hermes backend.
3. From the Desktop app, invoke the generic **Check for updates** action.
4. Observe that the result describes the remote container’s update policy rather than checking the locally installed Desktop application.

### Expected Behavior

Hermes Desktop should present two explicit, independently functioning targets:

- **Check for Desktop app updates** — checks the locally installed Electron application through the Desktop updater bridge, regardless of whether the active backend is local or remote.
- **Check for remote backend updates** — queries the remote backend, clearly labels it as the backend, and may correctly report that a managed/containerized backend cannot be updated from the app.

Connecting to a remote gateway should not disable or replace the local Desktop self-update check.

If a particular Desktop installation method cannot self-update, the app should identify that local installation method and provide the correct local update/reinstall instructions. It should not substitute the remote container’s message.

### Actual Behavior

In remote mode, the generic Desktop update action targets the backend. Against a managed cloud agent, the Desktop window reports:

```text
Update not available
Hermes updates are managed outside this dashboard in containerized environments.
```

The message does not say that only the **remote backend** is externally managed and does not answer whether the **Desktop app** itself has an update.

### Affected Component

Other, Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not uploaded. The behavior is deterministic UI routing and does not require cloud logs.
```

### Operating System

macos 26.5.2 (25F84)

### Python Version

N/A for the local packaged Electron client; remote backend Python is 3.13.5.

### Hermes Version

Hermes Desktop Version 0.19.0 (0.17.0) 

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Current `main` already models the Desktop client and backend as independently updatable states in:

```text
apps/desktop/src/store/updates.ts
```

It has distinct stores and check routines:

```ts
$updateStatus                 // local Desktop client
$backendUpdateStatus          // connected backend
checkUpdates()                // window.hermesDesktop.updates.check()
checkBackendUpdates()         // remote /api/hermes/update/check
```

However, the generic update entry points forcibly choose the backend whenever the connection is remote:

```ts
export function openUpdatesWindow(): void {
  openUpdateOverlayFor(isRemoteMode() ? 'backend' : 'client')
}

export function startActiveUpdate(): void {
  const target: UpdateTarget = isRemoteMode() ? 'backend' : 'client'
  // ...
}
```

Therefore, entering remote mode changes the meaning of the Desktop app’s generic update control from “update this Desktop application” to “update the connected backend.” The backend’s `can_apply=false` / container-management response is then presented inside the Desktop updater experience.

This is not merely a backend-detection bug: the hosted backend is correctly reporting that its image is managed externally. The error is that the Desktop UI selected the wrong update target for the user’s action and did not offer a separate local-client check.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

1. Replace the connection-mode-dependent single update target with two clearly labelled controls:
   - **Desktop app**
   - **Remote backend**
2. Keep **Check for Desktop updates** available in both local and remote modes and always route it to `checkUpdates()` / `window.hermesDesktop.updates.check()`.
3. Route backend checks only from an explicitly labelled backend control.
4. Display both client and backend version/status in the About or Updates panel.
5. When a managed backend returns `can_apply=false`, render: “Remote backend updates are managed by the hosting provider. This does not affect Desktop app updates.”
6. Never automatically apply a remote backend update from a generic Desktop update action; require a separately labelled confirmation.
7. Add a UI test for remote mode asserting that the local Desktop update control calls the Electron update bridge and not `/api/hermes/update/check`.
8. Add a second test asserting that the explicitly selected backend target does call the remote endpoint and safely displays the container-management message.

Related issues:

- #40018 — distinguishes Desktop self-update from optional remote-backend update and argues that remote updates require explicit opt-in and confirmation.
- #68517 — documents client/backend version skew and notes that a Desktop update affordance can update the remote backend while leaving the local client unchanged.
- #48594 — related `can_update_hermes` container messaging, but its host-classification bug is different; in this hosted incident, the backend really is container-managed.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

### Bug

Current `main` fails `tests/gateway/test_config.py::TestApiServerEnvOverride::test_env_key_does_not_reenable_explicitly_disabled_api_server`. The API-server enrollment hardening correctly changed env-based enrollment to require a usable key of at least 16 characters, but the older explicit-disable regression still supplies the weak fixture `secret-key`. `_apply_env_overrides()` therefore correctly ignores the key, while the stale assertion expects it to be stored.

### Reproduction

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_config.py
```

Observed on current `main` (`c4f5a45d5d9903998fb318ac6f3c5e6623e60445`) and in its CI. The same baseline failure blocks unrelated pull requests that include current main.

### Expected correction

Use a valid 16+ character test key and assert that value is preserved. Production behavior should remain unchanged.

items.title: cron: top-level delegate_task results are silently dropped, yet the job reports ok

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

When the model calls `delegate_task` inside a **cron job session**, the delegation results are silently dropped, yet the job finishes with `last_status: ok` and delivers only the model's "I'm waiting for the subagents…" narration text. The scheduled job's actual deliverable is never produced, and nothing surfaces the failure.

Observed on `v2026.7.7.2`, Ubuntu 24.04, gateway with in-process cron ticker.

## Mechanics (traced in v2026.7.7.2 source)

1. `cron/scheduler.py` builds cron sessions as `cron_{job_id}_{timestamp}` and runs the agent with `platform="cron"`.
2. Top-level model delegations are always forced to background — the schema-level `background` arg is intentionally ignored (`run_agent.py` `_dispatch_delegate_task`: `background=(not _is_subagent)`). So the model cannot opt into a synchronous delegation even if it wants to.
3. A cron session has no routing metadata, so when the delegation batch completes, the gateway drops the result: `gateway.run: Dropping watch notification with no routing metadata for process unknown`.
4. Meanwhile the parent turn has already ended (`reason=text_response`) with narration like "I've started 3 subagents in parallel, waiting for consolidated results…". The scheduler treats that text as the final result, delivers it, and marks the job `ok`.
5. The orphaned subagent sessions keep running and later fail with `run_agent: Session DB append_message failed: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'execute'` (writing against a closed DB connection). Their sessions stay `ended_at: NULL` in state.db.

Net effect: any cron job whose prompt (or the model's own initiative) leads to `delegate_task` produces a false-positive `ok` run with no deliverable — a silent failure mode that recurs daily and is invisible in `hermes cron list`.

## Reproduction sketch

Create a cron job whose prompt says "use delegate_task to parallelize" plus a final deliverable step (e.g. write a file and return a `MEDIA:` line). On execution: the tool dispatches an async batch, the turn ends with narration, the scheduler delivers the narration and records `ok`; the `MEDIA` step never runs. `agent.log` shows the `Dropping watch notification` line a few minutes later.

## Suggested fixes (any of these would close the hole)

- `cron/scheduler.py` already force-disables `cronjob`, `messaging` and `clarify` toolsets for cron runs — add `delegation` to that list (results can never route back, so the tool is a guaranteed trap in this context); **or**
- run top-level delegations synchronously when the session is a cron session (routing-less), instead of forcing background; **or**
- at minimum, mark the job run as failed (or annotate the delivery) when the run ends with an in-flight delegation batch whose results will be dropped, so the failure is visible.

Happy to provide more log excerpts if useful.

items.title: [Bug]: Multiple background process completions in same tick flood session with individual notifications instead of coalescing

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Description

When multiple background processes complete in the same gateway tick, each one delivers a separate notification into the agent session. This floods the context with redundant messages, causes session lag (`Persisted transcript lagged live cached history`), and leaves the agent processing notification-after-notification instead of responding to the user.

## Evidence

From gateway.log (6 processes completing at 17:24:53, all in the same second):

```
17:24:53.057 Process proc_99a794b9b5e9 finished — injecting agent notification
17:24:53.060 Process proc_ce2c0b31a186 finished — injecting agent notification
17:24:53.063 Process proc_12944841da9c finished — injecting agent notification
17:24:53.067 Process proc_7833aa6465b5 finished — injecting agent notification
17:24:53.070 Process proc_0f220e4e1655 finished — injecting agent notification
17:24:53.074 Process proc_d2824952ce08 finished — injecting agent notification
```

Then immediately after:

```
17:25:25 WARNING Persisted transcript lagged live cached history (disk=154, memory=157)
```

The session became unresponsive, with the user reporting "vc digita mas não termina nunca" (types forever but never finishes).

## Root cause

**Corrected — the original version of this issue blamed the wrong code path.**

I first attributed the flood to the post-turn drain loop over `_drain_gateway_watch_events()`. That was wrong. `_drain_gateway_watch_events()` forwards only `watch_match` and `watch_disabled` events, so standard process completions never reach it.

The flood comes from the **per-process watcher path**. The gateway starts one watcher per background process, and each watcher independently delivers its own completion notification when its process exits. Six processes finishing in the same second means six watchers each delivering once — six synthetic turns, no batching anywhere between them.

This is a code-level confirmation (read at `4c9628e`), not a measured one; I have not re-run the six-process reproduction end to end since correcting the diagnosis.

Consequence for anyone reading this issue for context: coalescing has to happen at the watcher/delivery seam. Batching in the drain loop cannot fix this, because the events are not there.

## Proposed fix

Fan in completions that share a delivery route inside a short window, and deliver one synthetic turn instead of N. Bound the rendering, and keep an aggregate summary so no result is silently lost:

```
[IMPORTANT: 6 background processes completed for this session.
Treat these results as one completion batch and send at most one
consolidated user-facing response.
  ...
Summary: 5 succeeded, 1 failed.]
```

The `watch_match` / `watch_disabled` events in the drain path have the same flood shape for a different reason and are worth coalescing too, but that is a second, independent problem — grouping there must use the full delivery routing key, not `session_key` alone, or events from different chats can merge into one misrouted message.

## Environment

- Hermes profile: `everton_full` (named profile)
- Platform: Discord (but issue is platform-agnostic)
- Config: `background_process_notifications: all` (default)
- OS: Linux

## Open PRs

- **#72675 — recommended merge candidate.** Coalesces at the watcher seam, `+327/-10`, two rounds of human review, three sweeper findings now fixed.
- #73469 — registry / state-machine approach, kept as draft. Removes the same failure modes structurally rather than pointwise, at `+1,120/-25`. The better design; the larger bet.
- #73547 — unrelated to the flood, but found in the same code: background process output reaches the platform unredacted when `security.redact_secrets` is disabled, because the terminal redactor is called without `force=True` on three user-facing sends.

I originally asked maintainers to choose between the first two. That was the wrong way to hand this over; the recommendation and its reasoning are in #72675.

items.title: Windows Desktop auto-update fails when gateway is running

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Bug: Windows Desktop auto-update breaks when gateway is running

When the Hermes Desktop app auto-updates on Windows, the update fails because the gateway process holds the venv lock, and the ZIP fallback deletes the pre-built desktop binary.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have the gateway running (`hermes gateway run`)
2. Open Hermes Desktop and trigger an update
3. Desktop detects pending commits, starts update
4. Update kills the backend, attempts to replace files
5. Fails: venv is locked by the gateway process

### What happens

**Phase 1 -- venv locked by gateway:**
The update process sees the venv is held open by the gateway:

```
[updates] venv shim still locked after 15s; aborting hand-off
[updates] error: Update aborted: another process is holding the Hermes install open
```

**Phase 2 -- ZIP download deletes pre-built desktop binary:**
The update falls back to ZIP download, which replaces `apps/desktop/` with source-only files. This deletes the pre-built `Hermes.exe` from `apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/`, so the desktop shortcut no longer works.

```
Failed to persist temporary file to ...venv\Lib\site-packages\..\..\Scripts\hermes.exe: access denied (os error 5)
```

### Aftermath
- Source code is updated correctly
- Python deps are NOT updated (pip install fails due to locked exe)
- `release/win-unpacked/Hermes.exe` is deleted (ZIP overwrites the dir)
- Desktop shortcut targets a non-existent binary -> app won't launch
- Gateway must be manually stopped and rebuilt: `hermes gateway stop && hermes update && hermes desktop --build-only && hermes gateway start`

### Expected behavior
1. Desktop auto-update should stop the gateway first (or refuse to update and tell the user why)
2. ZIP fallback should preserve the pre-built desktop binary, or the update flow should auto-rebuild it after extraction
3. Error message should point to the actual fix, not just "close other Hermes windows"

### Environment
- Windows 10 x64
- Hermes v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
- Git install
- Gateway platforms: Telegram + API Server

items.title: Gateway silently deaf after generic network loss — reconnect watcher never starts post-escalation (0.19.0)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Summary On 0.19.0 the gateway went silently deaf for ~22h after a plain Telegram network loss. `gateway_state` stayed `running` the whole time while `platforms.telegram.state` never returned to `connected`, and no messages were processed. The process was alive; nothing recovered it until an external restart. This is **not** the behind-a-proxy pool-timeout variant tracked in #69314 / draft #68983 — our error was a plain `httpx.ConnectError` (no proxy), for which `_looks_like_pool_timeout()` returns `False`, so that path is a no-op here. It also survived the cause-agnostic polling-recovery watchdog added in #67241 (which is in 0.19.0): the reconnect ladder did **not** stall mid-way — it completed all 10 attempts and escalated correctly, and the freeze happened **after** escalation. ### Version hermes-agent 0.19.0 (PyPI, installed via `uv tool`), macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5), Python 3.13. ### What the logs show `gateway.log` froze at `02:33:31`, and the **last** line written was the fatal-error log from `_handle_adapter_fatal_error_impl` (`gateway/run.py:4585`, `"Fatal %s adapter error"`) after the retryable escalation (`_set_fatal_error(..., retryable=True)`). The lines that should have followed were **never** written: - no bounded-disconnect timeout warning, - no `" queued for background reconnection"` (`gateway/run.py:4630`), - no `"Reconnecting telegram (attempt 1)..."` (`_platform_reconnect_watcher`, `gateway/run.py:8920`, logged *before* the connect attempt). So the background reconnect watcher never started a single attempt. Combined with the fact that every teardown await in the fatal handler is already bounded by `_await_adapter_cleanup_with_timeout` (`gateway/run.py:3796`), this looks like a **full event-loop freeze at ~02:33:31**, in the `run.py:4585 → 4630` window — not a single hung awaitable we can point to. We could not localize it further from logs alone. ### Reproduction Not deterministically reproduced — it followed a real, transient upstream network outage. We can share the surrounding `gateway.log` window on request. ### Requests / suggestions 1. **A stack dump at wedge time would localize this.** Would you consider a `faulthandler`/`py-spy`-style self-dump when the loop heartbeat stalls (or a `SIGQUIT` handler documented for operators), so a future occurrence is diagnosable? 2. **External detection signal that works today:** since `gateway_state` stays `running` throughout, a supervisor can detect this specifically via `platforms.

.state != connected` persisting past a threshold while `gateway_state` is `running`. We now restart on that condition externally; noting it in case it helps an internal watchdog design. 3. A separate, concrete residual gap we found while investigating (submitting as a small defense-in-depth PR, linked below): `_connect_adapter_with_timeout` (`gateway/run.py:3936`) still uses plain `asyncio.wait_for(adapter.connect(...))` rather than the detach-on-timeout helper used everywhere else, so a `connect()` that swallows `CancelledError` could wedge the reconnect watcher. **This is not the cause of the incident above** (the watcher never ran), but it is a real inconsistency worth closing. ### Search done Checked open + merged: #69314 (the proxy/pool-timeout variant), #67241 (the cause-agnostic polling-recovery watchdog, already in 0.19.0), plus sibling network-recovery issues on other platforms. None match this exact post-escalation freeze on a generic `ConnectError`.

items.title: OAuth credential pool enters unbounded, non-interruptible 401 retry loop (failed key hint matched no entry)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
## Severity
High — self-sustaining API retry loop that ignores stop signals; only an external process kill terminates it.

## Environment
- Profile: `default`, model `tencent/hy3:free` via provider `nous`
- Nous auth type: **OAuth token** (not a static API key). `shared/nous_auth.json` holds `access_token` / `refresh_token` / `client_id: hermes-cli` / `scope: inference:invoke`. No `NOUS_API_KEY` in `.env` or `config.yaml`.
- Config version: `_config_version: 33`
- `tool_loop_guardrails.hard_stop_enabled: false`; those guardrails only cover *tool-call* failures, not API/credential retries. `config.yaml` has no `retry`/`backoff`/`max_retries`/`pool` knob (verified by grep).

## Symptom
When the Nous inference endpoint returns an intermittent `401 - out of funds` (a transient auth glitch, not real depletion — 12 successful calls occurred in the same window), the agent enters a tight retry loop that:

1. Runs **without any user input** — `~1,524` rotate-without-marking events in ~4 minutes while the user was not responding. Not driven by user actions.
2. **Cannot be stopped via chat `/stop`** (or any chat command). The gateway logged:
   `gateway.run: Interrupt recursion depth 3 reached for session ... — queueing message instead of recursing.`
   i.e. the running loop never yielded to the interrupt; the user had to kill the gateway process in terminal.
3. Only terminated by manually killing the gateway process.

Log evidence (`~/.hermes/logs/agent.log`, default profile):
- `1,524` occurrences of: `credential pool: failed key hint matched no nous entry; rotating without marking any credential exhausted` (~20:09:26 → 20:13:50, ≈6/sec).
- Errors log packed with `Streaming attempt superseded by a newer stream` / `Discarding chunk from superseded stream attempt`.
- `gateway.run: Interrupt recursion depth 3 reached ... queueing message instead of recursing`

## Root cause
`agent/credential_pool.py` → `mark_exhausted_and_rotate()` (≈ lines 1768–1841):

```python
if api_key_hint:
    entry = next((e for e in self._entries if e.runtime_api_key == api_key_hint), None)
    if entry is None:
        # failed key is identifiable but matches no entry
        logger.info("credential pool: failed key hint matched no %s entry; "
                    "rotating without marking any credential exhausted", self.provider)
        self._current_id = None
        return self._select_unlocked()   # <-- returns the SAME token
```

For OAuth-token auth, the upstream 401's `api_key_hint` never matches a pool entry's `runtime_api_key`, so the code takes the `entry is None` branch, deliberately **does not mark anything exhausted**, and returns `_select_unlocked()` — the same still-failing token. Caller retries → same 401 → same branch → forever. No backoff, no cap.

The function's own sibling comment (≈ lines 1798–1808) documents the related failure class:
> "...rotation never converges — the caller `continue`s forever until the client disconnects (a ~2.5min hang with no error surfaced to the user)."

The OAuth no-match branch has no such bounded escape, so the loop can run until the process is killed.

Compounding factors:
- No backoff between rotations → ~6 iter/sec, starving the event loop so chat interrupts can't be processed (gateway hits recursion depth 3 and queues instead of recursing).
- `tool_loop_guardrails.hard_stop_enabled: false`.

## Impact
- User cannot stop the loop from chat; requires terminal process kill.
- Pointless retry churn; masks real outages and can waste quota on metered providers.
- A genuine 401 (expired OAuth that refresh can't fix, or truly out-of-funds) hangs instead of surfacing a clean error.

## Suggested fixes
1. **Bound the no-match branch.** After N consecutive no-mark rotations for the same provider in a short window, mark the credential `DEAD` (or reach the "no available entries" state) so the error propagates instead of looping.
2. **Add backoff/cooldown** between rotation attempts (fixed sleep or exponential) so the loop yields to interrupts.
3. **Treat OAuth-token 401 as terminal after refresh fails.** If `try_refresh_current()` can't restore a valid token, surface the auth error rather than retrying the dead token.
4. **Wire API-level retries into the guardrail system** (or add a user-tunable `max_api_retries` / `api_retry_backoff`) bounded by default.

## Reproduction
- Default profile on Nous OAuth auth.
- Trigger an intermittent `401` from the Nous inference endpoint during a stream (transient auth blip, or expired token mid-session).
- Observe `failed key hint matched no nous entry; rotating without marking...` repeating without end; `/stop` in chat will not terminate it.

## False positives ruled out
- The startup `⚠ TERMINAL_CWD=/Users/julie found in .env — deprecated` warning is a **false positive**: it matches a *commented-out* line (`# TERMINAL_CWD=.`) in `.env`; the real value is correctly `terminal.cwd: .` in `config.yaml`. Not related to this bug.
- The `$18.37/$22` banner is cosmetic per-session, not a live spend meter.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — clicking a chat session from Kanban/Artifacts does not return to chat (forced to New session)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

In Hermes Desktop (macOS), after opening **Kanban** or **Artifacts**, clicking an existing **chat session** in the sidebar does **not** return the main workspace to that chat.

The user is stuck on the Kanban/Artifacts page. The only reliable escape is clicking **New session**, which loses the intent to resume the existing conversation.

This is an urgent navigation bug: sidebar session rows look clickable but fail to restore the chat surface when a full-page view is active.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop on macOS with at least one existing chat session in the sidebar.
2. Optionally open that session once so it is the active/selected main session.
3. Navigate to **Artifacts** (sidebar nav) **or** **Kanban** (sidebar contributed route / plugin page).
4. Confirm the main pane shows Artifacts or Kanban (full page, not chat).
5. Click the existing chat session row in the sidebar.
6. **Observe:** main pane stays on Artifacts/Kanban; chat does not appear.
7. Click **New session** → chat UI returns (workaround), but not the intended session resume path.

Also verify:

- Click session A while on Artifacts when session B was last active.
- Click the same session that is already selected while on Kanban.
- Session row click should always route to chat for that session id.

### Expected Behavior

Clicking a sidebar chat session **always**:

1. Navigates the app route back to the chat session (`sessionRoute(sessionId)`), and
2. Shows that session’s transcript + composer in the main workspace, and
3. Clears full-page workspace modes (Artifacts / Kanban / Skills / Messaging / contributed pages).

No need to click New session.

### Actual Behavior

- Sidebar session click while on Kanban/Artifacts often does nothing visible to the main pane.
- User remains on Kanban/Artifacts.
- Forced workaround: **New session** (wrong).

### Affected Component

- Desktop app navigation / sessions sidebar / workspace full-page views
- Routes: `/artifacts`, contributed `/kanban` (and likely any `$workspaceIsPage === true` route)
- Not CLI

### Root Cause Analysis (high confidence from current main)

Session row click → `onResume()` → `onResumeSession(sessionId)` in wiring:

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/wiring.tsx
onResumeSession: sessionId => {
  if (!focusOpenSession(sessionId)) {
    navigate(sessionRoute(sessionId))
  }
},
```

`focusOpenSession` (`apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts`):

```ts
export function focusOpenSession(storedSessionId: string): boolean {
  if ($sessionTiles.get().some(t => t.storedSessionId === storedSessionId)) {
    revealTreePane(paneId)
    // ...
    return true  // ← navigates NOTHING
  }

  if (storedSessionId === $selectedStoredSessionId.get()) {
    revealTreePane('workspace')
    // ...
    return true  // ← navigates NOTHING
  }

  return false
}
```

When the clicked session is **already the selected main session** (common) or already opened as a tile, `focusOpenSession` returns `true` and **skips `navigate(sessionRoute(sessionId))`**.

Meanwhile Artifacts/Kanban are **full-page workspace routes** gated by:

- `apps/desktop/src/app/routes.ts` → `ARTIFACTS_ROUTE = '/artifacts'`, contributed routes e.g. `/kanban`
- `appViewForPath` / `$workspaceIsPage` / `syncWorkspaceIsPage(pathname)`
- `headerVeto` while page is active (`apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/controller.tsx`)

Revealing the workspace pane without changing the **router pathname** leaves the user on `/artifacts` or `/kanban`. The click feels dead.

**Bug class:** “focus already-open session” optimization does not account for **workspace full-page views**. Same class will affect Skills / Messaging / any `sidebar.nav` contributed page.

### Proposed Fix

Minimal correct fix:

```ts
onResumeSession: sessionId => {
  const focused = focusOpenSession(sessionId)
  // Always leave full-page views (artifacts/kanban/skills/...).
  if (!focused || $workspaceIsPage.get()) {
    navigate(sessionRoute(sessionId))
  }
}
```

Or push into a shared `resumeSessionFromSidebar(sessionId)` helper used by every entry point:

1. If `$workspaceIsPage.get()`, **always** `navigate(sessionRoute(sessionId))`.
2. Still call tile focus/reveal logic so split tiles behave.
3. Ensure `syncWorkspaceIsPage` clears `headerVeto` after navigation.
4. Audit other callers that short-circuit on `focusOpenSession` (command palette, notifications, deep links).

### Tests to add

| Area | Assertion |
|------|-----------|
| wiring / extracted helper | When pathname is `/artifacts` and selected session is S, `onResumeSession(S)` navigates to `sessionRoute(S)` |
| same | When pathname is `/kanban` (contributed), resume navigates to chat |
| `session-states` / callers | focus helper does not claim “done” while workspace is a page **or** callers always navigate on page |
| routes | `appViewForPath(sessionRoute(id)) === 'chat'`; `$workspaceIsPage` false after nav |
| e2e if present | `apps/desktop/e2e`: artifacts → click session → composer visible |

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] From **Artifacts**, click any sidebar chat session → that chat is shown immediately
- [ ] From **Kanban**, click any sidebar chat session → that chat is shown immediately
- [ ] Works for the already-selected session and for a different session
- [ ] Works when the session is open as a tile and when it is only in the main workspace
- [ ] New session is no longer required as a workaround
- [ ] Same fix covers other full-page views (Skills, Messaging, contributed pages) unless intentionally excluded
- [ ] Unit/integration tests prevent regression

### Operating System

macOS — Hermes Desktop

### Debug Report

Deterministic UI navigation bug; no backend logs required. After a failed click, active route stays `/artifacts` or `/kanban`.

### Priority

**Urgent / P0–P1.** Breaks primary navigation loop between tools and chats.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — cannot scroll up in some chat sessions
items.body:
### Bug Description

In some chat sessions (often ones that already feel “buggy” / wedged), the transcript **cannot be scrolled upward**. Older messages are unreachable. High priority — breaks review of prior context.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop.
2. Enter an affected session (long thread and/or session that hit errors / partial load / remote).
3. Attempt to scroll up via trackpad, mouse wheel, or scrollbar.
4. **Observe:** scroll does not move up, rubber-bands, or immediately snaps back to bottom.

### Expected Behavior

- User can always scroll to older messages when content overflows.
- Stick-to-bottom only holds while user is at bottom; intentional upward scroll releases the pin.
- No session state should permanently disable upward scroll.

### Actual Behavior

Upward scroll fails in affected sessions; user stuck at bottom (or cannot move).

### Affected Component

Desktop chat thread scroller (`apps/desktop`)

### Root Cause Hints

| Area | Path |
|------|------|
| Thread list / stick-to-bottom | `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/list.tsx` — `useStickToBottom`, comments about single scroll owner, `overflow-anchor` |
| Scroll store | `apps/desktop/src/store/thread-scroll.ts` — `resetThreadScroll`, `onScrollToBottomRequest` |
| Loading overlay interaction | `thread-loading.ts` + chat shell — loader may capture pointer / lock layout |
| Virtualization / content-visibility | thread list + markdown `content-visibility` — height mismeasure can break scroll range |

Likely classes: stick-to-bottom not releasing; scrollHeight stuck because loader/spacer; overflow hidden on wrong ancestor; session switch leaving scroll lock true.

### Proposed Fix

1. Reproduce with long transcript + working/loading flags; verify `useStickToBottom` release on wheel up.
2. Ensure loading overlays are `pointer-events-none` where appropriate and don’t zero out scroll range.
3. On session switch, reset scroll lock sanely but allow immediate user scroll up.
4. Add regression test or e2e: seed long messages → wheel up → `scrollTop` decreases and stays.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Can scroll to top on long sessions
- [ ] Stick-to-bottom still works for live streaming when user is at bottom
- [ ] Affected “buggy” sessions recoverable without New session

### Operating System

macOS — Hermes Desktop

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — viewing/opening a chat marks it idle/done while the session is still in progress

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

Opening or viewing a chat session that is **still running** incorrectly marks it as **done / idle** in the sidebar (working indicator clears) even though the agent turn is still in progress.

High priority — users lose the signal that work is ongoing; easy to interrupt or abandon live runs.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long-running turn in session A (tools/streaming still active).
2. Confirm sidebar shows working state (dot/arc).
3. Switch away, then **open/view session A again** (or simply select it while it runs).
4. **Observe:** working indicator clears / session looks finished (“done”) while the run continues (or content still streaming).

### Expected Behavior

- Working/busy state is **authoritative from backend/runtime**, not cleared merely because the user focused the session.
- Viewing a session may clear **unread-finished** badges, but must **not** clear **in-progress working** state.
- Sidebar, tab dot, and composer busy UI stay consistent while the turn runs.

### Actual Behavior

Viewing/opening clears the in-progress affordance; session appears done while still working.

### Affected Component

Desktop session live state (`apps/desktop`)

### Root Cause Hints

| Area | Path | Notes |
|------|------|--------|
| Unread clear on open | `apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts` — `setSelectedStoredSessionId` clears `$unreadFinishedSessionIds` | Correct for unread; must not be conflated with working |
| Working ids | `apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts` — `$workingSessionIds` derived from per-session busy |
| Busy updates | session state merge on resume/events — resume payload may set `busy: false` stale |
| Dot UI | `session-status-dot.tsx` / `session-row.tsx` | Renders from working/unread atoms |

Likely: `session.resume` snapshot overwrites live busy=false; or focus path clears working set; or unread-green→idle is misread but actual busy also drops — fix must preserve busy from stream/watchdog until turn terminal event.

### Proposed Fix

1. On resume/open, **merge** busy/working from live runtime; do not clobber true busy with stale resume snapshot.
2. Split “unread finished” clear (OK on view) from “working” clear (only on turn end / explicit interrupt).
3. Add test: session busy true → select/open → still in `$workingSessionIds` until busy false event.
4. Verify remote gateway event ordering under latency.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening an in-progress chat keeps working indicator
- [ ] Unread-finished still clears on view when turn actually completed in background
- [ ] No false “done” while tools/LLM still running
- [ ] Tests lock the invariant

### Operating System

macOS — Hermes Desktop

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — relative timestamps (sidebar + in-chat) should show exact time on hover
items.body:
### Bug Description

Hermes Desktop shows **relative** times in two places:

1. **Sidebar session rows** — e.g. `7h` / `7h ago` on hover of the row
2. **Inside the chat transcript** — e.g. `7h ago` on the message age control

In both places, continuing to hover (or focusing) the relative time should reveal the **exact local date/time** (e.g. `6:53 PM, Jul 22, 2026`). Today this is missing or unreliable.

**Priority:** High  
**Scope:** Both sidebar **and** in-chat (not one or the other).

### Steps to Reproduce

**A — Sidebar**
1. Open Desktop with sessions old enough to show a relative age.
2. Hover the session row so the relative age appears (e.g. `7h`).
3. Hover that age label / keep hovering.
4. **Observe:** no reliable exact timestamp tooltip.

**B — In-chat**
1. Open a chat whose messages show relative age (e.g. `7h ago`) on the message chrome.
2. Hover the relative age label.
3. **Observe:** no clear exact timestamp (native `title` missing, delayed, or never useful).

### Expected Behavior

- Relative label stays compact (`7h` / `7h ago`).
- Hover **and** keyboard focus show exact local time via a real Desktop tooltip (not only a flaky native `title` delay), e.g.:
  - `Today at 6:53 PM`
  - `Yesterday at 6:53 PM`
  - `Jul 22, 2026, 6:53 PM` (locale-aware)
- Same quality of affordance in **sidebar** and **in-chat**.

### Actual Behavior

Relative times only (or absolute only via unreliable native tooltip). Exact time not practically discoverable.

### Affected Component

Desktop UI timestamps — sidebar session rows + in-thread message age (`apps/desktop`)

### Root Cause Hints

| Surface | Path | Notes |
|---------|------|--------|
| Sidebar age | `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-row.tsx` — `formatAge(...)` | Age `<span>` is `pointer-events-none` → hover cannot target it for a tooltip |
| Sidebar age source | `session.last_active \|\| session.started_at` (unix seconds) | |
| In-chat age | `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/assistant-message.tsx` — `MessageAge` | Uses `formatAgo`; sets native `title={formatMessageTimestamp(...)}` only |
| Absolute formatter (exists) | `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/timestamp.ts` — `formatMessageTimestamp` | Today / Yesterday / `fmtDayTime` |
| Time utils | `apps/desktop/src/lib/time.ts` — `formatAgo`, `fmtClock`, `fmtDayTime`, `coarseElapsed` |
| Formatter tests | `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/timestamp.test.ts` | |
| Tooltip primitive | Desktop `Tip` / tooltip used elsewhere in sidebar | Prefer this over native `title` in Electron |

Likely gaps:
1. Sidebar: `pointer-events-none` on age prevents hover tooltip entirely.
2. In-chat: native HTML `title` is delayed/unreliable in Electron/macOS.
3. Missing `createdAt` on some runtime messages → `MessageAge` returns null.
4. No shared helper wiring absolute tooltip on both surfaces.

### Proposed Fix

1. **Shared helper** (optional but clean): `absoluteTimeLabel(ms | Date)` reusing `formatMessageTimestamp` / `fmtDayTime`.
2. **Sidebar:** remove `pointer-events-none` from age (or wrap a hoverable target); attach `Tip` with absolute time from `last_active` / `started_at`.
3. **In-chat:** wrap `MessageAge` with the same `Tip` (keep relative `formatAgo` as visible text).
4. Ensure history hydrate populates `createdAt` so in-chat age appears consistently.
5. User-message age: if shown anywhere, same tooltip behavior.
6. Tests: both surfaces expose tooltip/accessible description with absolute time; keep `formatMessageTimestamp` unit tests.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sidebar: hover relative session age → exact local date/time
- [ ] In-chat: hover relative message age → exact local date/time
- [ ] Tooltips reliable on macOS Desktop (not depending on slow native `title` alone)
- [ ] Keyboard focus works where applicable
- [ ] No layout shift; relative label stays compact
- [ ] Tests cover both surfaces

### Operating System

macOS — Hermes Desktop

### Note

This issue intentionally covers **both** sidebar and in-chat. Do not close as “sidebar only” or “in-chat only.”

items.title: Session hangs forever (no output) when history has a blank assistant text block + tool_calls — HTTP 400 replays every turn; sessions repair only fixes schema

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

A long-running session can hang with no response — the agent looks like it's "thinking" forever and never produces output. Root cause: an assistant message persisted with **empty/whitespace-only content while it carries `tool_calls`** serializes to an empty text content block, and Anthropic (and Bedrock) reject the whole request:

```
HTTP 400: messages: text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text
```

Because the blank block lives in **stored history**, it replays on every subsequent turn, so the session stays wedged behind the same 400. The failure is silent from the user's side: no console output, no error surfaced in the UI, the turn just dies.

## Why the existing fix doesn't cover it

The request-path adapters already coerce empty/whitespace text blocks on send (#69512, `anthropic_adapter._safe_text` / the final content walk in `_convert_assistant_message`). That prevents *new* blanks from going out. But rows **persisted before that coercion existed** are still in the DB, and depending on the serialization path they can still reach the wire — leaving old sessions permanently stuck.

`hermes sessions repair` exists, but it only handles **schema-level** corruption (`_db_opens_cleanly` / `repair_state_db_schema`: does the DB open, are the FTS indexes intact). It has no path for **content-level** poison like this.

## Reproduction (shape)

1. A session accumulates assistant turns that are pure tool calls (the model calls a tool and says nothing) — these get stored with empty `content` plus a `tool_calls` array.
2. On a build/serialization path that emits the empty text block, the next request 400s with "text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text".
3. Every retry re-sends the same history → same 400 → the session hangs indefinitely.

Observed on a real install: thousands of such rows across dozens of sessions, each with `content = ''`/`NULL` and a populated `tool_calls`. Manually coercing the blank `content` to any non-whitespace string immediately unwedged the affected sessions.

## Proposed fix

Extend the existing repair command with a content-level pass:

- `repair_blank_message_content(db_path, check_only=, backup=)` in `hermes_state.py`: heals assistant rows that are **both** blank-text **and** tool-call-bearing, rewriting only their `content` to a non-whitespace placeholder. Tool_use payloads and every other message are untouched. Whitespace matching uses the full space/tab/newline/CR set (SQLite `trim()` strips only ASCII space by default), matching the adapter's `str.strip()` coercion.
- Wire it into `hermes sessions repair --content` (honors `--check-only` and `--no-backup`, takes a timestamped backup by default).

PR: (link below).

## Environment

- Providers: Anthropic (native) and Bedrock reject blank text blocks; the poison is provider-agnostic once stored.
- Reproduced on current `main`.

---
*Filed during triage of a real hang; root cause confirmed against stored message rows and the backend 400s.*

items.title: Docker image ships WAL-reset-vulnerable SQLite (Debian trixie libsqlite3 3.46.1) — no fixed-SQLite path for image installs (parity with #70200/#70186)

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

items.body:
The official image (`FROM debian:13.4`, apt `python3`, venv via `uv sync` on the system interpreter) dynamically links `libsqlite3-0 3.46.1-7+deb13u1`, which `hermes doctor` itself flags as vulnerable to the WAL-reset corruption bug (https://sqlite.org/wal.html#walresetbug, fixed 3.51.3+, backports 3.50.7 / 3.44.6). Debian trixie carries no backport (its latest changelog entry, 2026-01-22, only addresses CVE-2025-7709), so `docker pull` + recreate keeps shipping the vulnerable library indefinitely.

#70200 / #70186 repair managed (uv / python-build-standalone) installs, but image installs have no equivalent path; the #70055 DELETE-mode gate protects only NEW shared DBs, so pre-existing WAL databases (`kanban.db`, `state.db`) on busy multi-worker boards still ride the vulnerable checkpoint path — we have observed live `kanban.db` corruption fences on 0.19.0 under concurrent-worker load.

**Request:** bake a fixed SQLite (>= 3.51.3; #70200 targets 3.53.1) into the published image — e.g. compile the pinned autoconf amalgamation into `/usr/local/lib/<multiarch>` ahead of the distro lib, or install a fixed `libsqlite3-0` — and/or document an endorsed override for derived images.

Happy to share our derived-image layer (pinned 3.53.3 build with SHA3 verification and build-time version/FTS5 asserts) as a reference.

items.title: [Feature]: Memory tool needs a pre-write gate — skill content leaks into memory due to friction asymmetry

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
## Problem

The `memory` tool has zero friction — one `memory(action="add")` call and content is persisted. The `skill_manage` tool requires matching `old_string` for patches and correct SKILL.md formatting. This **friction asymmetry** creates a structural vulnerability:

1. Agent completes complex work (e.g., upgrading a skill)
2. Agent wants to "save what I learned"
3. Memory is the path of least resistance — one tool call, no pattern matching
4. Methodology, version notes, and skill-level content flow into memory instead of skills

Even with clear rules in memory itself (e.g., "does forgetting this cause mistakes? → memory. Will you follow this next time? → skill"), the agent under cognitive load skips the classification step and defaults to memory.

## Real-world impact

A user session accumulated 19 memory entries of AI-writing methodology that duplicated content already in their skills. All 19 were redundant — the skill already had this information. Manual cleanup was required.

## Proposed solution

Add a **configurable pre-write gate** to the `memory` tool:

### Option A: Write justification mode (configurable)
`memory.require_justification: true` — each memory write must include a `category` field (`decision_rule` / `user_preference` / `environment`) that forces the agent to classify before writing. If the agent can't classify it, it shouldn't write it.

### Option B: Write confirmation mode (simple)
`memory.confirm_writes: true` — the tool returns a non-final response asking "Are you sure? This content will persist across sessions." The agent must call `memory(action="confirm")` to complete the write.

### Option C: Friction parity
Make memory writes match the friction level of skill writes. E.g., require a `reason` field that explains why this belongs in memory vs skill.

## Why this matters

This is not a "better prompt" problem. The agent already has clear classification rules in memory. The issue is **structural**: when two tools have asymmetric friction, content flows to the easier one regardless of rules. Adding a gate to the easier tool restores the balance.

items.title: Telegram overflow split produces duplicate message storms under flood control

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
## Summary
When a long message triggers the `_edit_overflow_split` path in `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`, hitting Telegram's flood control causes a destructive retry cascade that sends duplicates — observed up to **32 copies** of the same message.

## Root Cause
The continuation send loop in `_edit_overflow_split()` (line ~2940) fires chunks at network speed with **no flood-control awareness**. When Telegram responds with `RetryAfter`, the chunk is silently dropped, the entire split operation returns partial failure, and the streaming engine retries the edit from scratch. On retry, chunk 1 is detected as "not modified" (already sent) and passes through, but chunks 2-N fire again — hitting flood control again — creating the loop.

Compare: `edit_message()` (line 2805) **does** handle `RetryAfter` properly — it `await asyncio.sleep(wait)`, retries once, and returns a clean failure for long waits so streaming falls back gracefully. The overflow split continuation loop has none of this.

## Evidence
- **26 flood control errors** logged in `errors.log` since July 6, 2026
- Error pattern: `"Overflow continuation send failed: Flood control exceeded"` and `"Flood control exceeded. Retry in 223 seconds"`
- Cascading retries producing duplicate message storms
- Observed on hermes-agent **v0.17.0**, running on a cloud VPS (Linux, Python 3.11.15)

## Relevant Code
`gateway/platforms/telegram.py` — `_edit_overflow_split()` method, the continuation send loop starting around line 2940. The fix should mirror the flood-control handling already present in `edit_message()` (lines 2805–2830): catch `RetryAfter`, sleep inline for short waits, and return a clean failure for long waits so the streaming engine falls back to a `send_message` instead of retrying the edit cascade.

## Repro
1. Send a message long enough to trigger overflow split (e.g., a large markdown table with 50+ rows)
2. Gateway splits into N chunks, fires continuation sends rapidly
3. Telegram hits flood control → retry cascade → duplicates

## Impact
Severe: users see dozens of duplicate messages, making conversation threads unreadable. The user reported seeing the same chapter repeated "like a hundred times."

items.title: Desktop: stale truncate_before_user_ordinal on prompt.submit can silently wipe an entire session transcript

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

The desktop "rewind / regenerate / restore from this message" flow sends `prompt.submit` with a `truncate_before_user_ordinal` computed from the **frontend's local message list**. The backend (`tui_gateway/server.py`) applies that ordinal directly against its own in-memory history and persists the truncation with `replace_messages()` — which physically DELETEs every row after the cut point from `state.db`. When the two views desync (frontend holding a partial/stale/empty transcript), a perfectly ordinary user action can wipe an entire session's history. This happened to me in production: **308 messages of a session were silently and unrecoverably deleted.**

## Environment

- Hermes desktop 0.18.2 (release 2026.7.7.2), macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon)
- Backend running from repo checkout, commit `a7a696ba5`

## Real-world incident (2026-07-23, all times local)

1. Session `20260723_073515_5dab27` had been active since 07:35, ~308 history entries (`agent.log` turn_context shows `history=308` at 13:44).
2. 14:04 — I opened a **new** session and submitted a prompt; the model stream stalled. At 14:08:11 I interrupted it (`interrupted_during_api_call`).
3. ~14:08 — I switched back to the old session's tab and sent a fresh, newly-typed message.
4. 14:08:28 — the turn started with `history=0`. The session's entire prior transcript was gone from `state.db` (and from `messages_fts`), with **no log line anywhere** recording the deletion.
5. `sessions.rewind_count` stayed 0; no compression counters moved. A whole-DB audit shows this is the only session affected since 07-15.

Concurrent `desktop.log` renderer errors from the same period suggest the frontend transcript view was corrupted at the time:

```
Uncaught Error: useClientLookup: Index 0 out of bounds (length: 0)
Uncaught Error: Composer is not available
```

## Root cause

`tui_gateway/server.py`, `prompt.submit` handler:

```python
truncate_user_ordinal = params.get("truncate_before_user_ordinal")
...
history = session.get("history", [])
user_indices = [i for i, m in enumerate(history) if m.get("role") == "user"]
if ordinal < 0 or ordinal >= len(user_indices):
    return _err(rid, 4018, ...)
truncated = history[: user_indices[ordinal]]
session["history"] = truncated
...
db.replace_messages(session["session_key"], truncated)   # DELETEs all other rows
```

`replace_messages` (`hermes_state.py`) is documented as *"DESTRUCTIVE by default: every row for the session is DELETEd (and drops out of the FTS index)"*.

The ordinal is an **index into the frontend's message array** (`use-prompt-actions/rewind.ts` et al. compute it via `qqi(messages, i)` on the client). The backend treats it as an index into its own history. These are only guaranteed to agree if the client's transcript view is perfectly in sync. In the incident, a stale `truncate_before_user_ordinal=0` rode along with an ordinary fresh submit; `history[:user_indices[0]]` evaluated to `[]`, and `replace_messages(session, [])` erased everything.

Note the existing bounds check only protects against *out-of-range* ordinals. `ordinal=0` is always in range and always means "delete the entire transcript" — an outcome that has no legitimate use for a plain prompt submit, yet requires no confirmation and produces no log.

## Impact

- Silent, unrecoverable loss of a complete session transcript (messages + FTS rows; nothing in freelist recoverable, no `state.db` backups exist).
- Any frontend desync (renderer errors, tab restore with partial history, backend restart leaving client state stale) can trigger it through rewind/regenerate/restore/edit-resend — or, as here, an ordinary submit carrying a stale truncation plan.

## Related work

This is the same bug class as #69107 / #69109, but the **opposite desync direction** and a worse outcome:

- #69107: the *backend's* in-memory history is stale relative to the DB → a valid ordinal is rejected (4018) or newer rows are discarded. #69109 fixes that by re-reading fresh history before validating.
- **This issue**: the backend's in-memory history was perfectly fresh (it had just served a `history=308` turn), but the *frontend's* ordinal was garbage — a stale `truncate_before_user_ordinal=0` attached to an ordinary fresh submit. Re-reading fresh history (the #69109 fix) would **not** have prevented it: `history[:user_indices[0]]` still evaluates to `[]` and `replace_messages(session, [])` still erases everything. The missing pieces are (a) a guard on the empty-truncation edge, (b) an integrity check tying the ordinal to something the backend can verify, and (c) any logging of the destructive rewrite.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Identify the cut point by stable message id, not ordinal.** The client should send the target message's id; the backend resolves its position in its own history. If the id isn't found, reject.
2. **Validate `history_version`.** The backend already bumps `session["history_version"]` on truncation; have the client echo the version its view is based on and reject mismatches.
3. **Guard the empty-truncation edge.** Refuse `truncated == []` unless an explicit `confirm_empty_truncate=true` is passed; log every truncation (`history N -> M, ordinal=k`) so future incidents are traceable.
4. Longer term: keep a tombstone/backup before destructive rewrites (or make `archive_and_compact` the only truncation path), so a bad rewrite is recoverable.

## Local mitigation (applied on my install, for reference)

Backend-only guard in `prompt.submit`, right after `truncated = history[...]`:

```python
if not truncated and not params.get("confirm_empty_truncate"):
    logger.warning(
        "prompt.submit: REFUSED empty truncation of session %s "
        "(%d messages would be wiped; ordinal=%d).",
        sid, len(history), ordinal,
    )
    return _err(rid, 4019,
        "truncation would erase the entire session transcript; "
        "resubmit with confirm_empty_truncate=true if this is intended")
logger.warning(
    "prompt.submit: truncating session %s history %d -> %d messages (ordinal=%d)",
    sid, len(history), len(truncated), ordinal,
)
```

This blocks the observed wipe shape while leaving ordinary rewinds (`ordinal > 0`) untouched; happy to open a PR with it if useful.

items.body:
### Feature Request

Currently session archiving (via `hermes sessions prune` or any future archive mechanism) either keeps a session fully visible in the GUI session list or deletes it entirely. There is no middle ground.

### Desired Behavior

When a session is archived:
1. It is **hidden from the GUI session list** (`hermes sessions list` / desktop sidebar) — declutters the active view
2. It remains **fully searchable via `session_search`** — the FTS5 index still covers archived sessions
3. (Optional) A filter toggle in GUI like "Show archived sessions" to unhide them on demand

### Use Case

Users who have years of conversation history want to keep every session for future retrieval (session_search is powerful for this), but do not want thousands of old sessions cluttering the desktop sidebar or CLI list. This is analogous to email archiving — the message is not deleted, just hidden from the inbox.

### Suggested Implementation

- Add an `archived_at` timestamp column (nullable) to the sessions table in state.db
- `hermes sessions archive <id>` sets `archived_at` to now (new CLI subcommand or flag)
- GUI session list / `hermes sessions list` filters out rows where `archived_at IS NOT NULL` by default
- `session_search` continues to search across all sessions (or accepts an `include_archived` filter)
- Desktop GUI could add a "Show archived" checkbox or filter

Related: PR #59426 (Codex-style archiving), Issue #69322 (archived session visibility)

items.title: Feature: Harness-level ANSI/escape sequence sanitization for tool results

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Feature Request: Harness-Level ANSI/Escape Sequence Sanitization for Tool Results

### Problem
MCP tool outputs (and other external tool results) can contain ANSI escape sequences, OSC sequences, zero-width characters, and other control characters that constitute an **output injection attack vector**. A compromised or malicious MCP server can return crafted output that:
- Manipulates terminal rendering (screen clearing `\x1b[2J`, cursor positioning `\x1b[1;1H`, color changes)
- Injects invisible Unicode (bidi overrides `\u202e`, zero-width joiners `\u200d`, ZWSP `\u200b`) that affect model interpretation
- Masquerades as legitimate output while hiding malicious content

### Current State
- No harness-level sanitization exists for tool results before they enter model context or display
- The `transform_tool_result` plugin hook exists (added in v0.11.0) but requires users to install a plugin
- Plugin-based defense is opt-in, not default

### Proposed Solution
Add **built-in, default-on sanitization** in the tool result pipeline (likely in `model_tools.py` where `transform_tool_result` fires, or in the tool dispatcher post-execution) that strips:
1. **ANSI CSI sequences** — SGR colors, cursor movement, screen erase, etc.
2. **ANSI OSC sequences** — Window titles, hyperlinks, etc.
3. **C0 control characters** — `\x00-\x08`, `\x0b`, `\x0c`, `\x0e-\x1f` (preserving `\t`, `\n`, `\r`)
4. **DEL character** — `\x7f`
5. **Zero-width / bidi override Unicode** — `\u200b-\u200f`, `\u202a-\u202e`, `\u2060-\u2064`, `\ufeff`

This should happen **before**:
- Tool result enters conversation context (model sees clean output)
- Tool result is rendered to display/terminal

### Reference Implementation
A working local plugin demonstrating the sanitization logic exists at `~/.hermes/plugins/mcp-sanitizer/`:

```python
_ANSI_CSI_RE = re.compile(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*[mGKHfABCDsuJK]')
_ANSI_OSC_RE = re.compile(r'\x1b\][^\x07\x1b]*[\x07\x1b]')
_C0_CONTROLS_RE = re.compile(r'[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f]')
_DEL_RE = re.compile(r'\x7f')
_ZW_CHARS_RE = re.compile(r'[\u200b-\u200f\u202a-\u202e\u2060-\u2064\ufeff]')
```

### Why This Belongs in Core
Per MCP security best practices: *"The actual fix is stripping escape sequences before rendering and before the model sees them, and honestly that belongs in the harness, not in your morning routine. It's a client-layer job."*

The existing `strip_ansi()` utility (commit `934fbe3c`) used for ShellFileOperations should be extended and applied universally at the harness level.

### Related Issues
- #18981 — No harness-level defense against prompt injection in tool outputs
- #8933 — `transform_tool_result` plugin hook (the extension point this would use)
- #5400 — HERMES_FENCE markers leak (shows ANSI/control char handling gaps)
- #31816 — `hermes update` emits ANSI demo in non-interactive logs

items.body:
## Symptom

`e2e/session-compression-and-queue-stop.spec.ts:118` — "session compression in progress › queues an Enter-submitted draft instead of steering while compaction is active" — times out at the 90s test budget, including on Playwright's automatic retry.

Observed 5 consecutive failures within ~45 minutes on 2026-07-24, across three unrelated docs/skills-only PRs (#70512, #70519, #70531 — none touch desktop code) **and on main itself** (commit 3910ab28, run 30063335713). The sibling spec at `:52` ("compresses an existing session and accepts a follow-up turn") also failed once and passed on retry — same underlying race, lower frequency.

Because `Desktop E2E / Playwright E2E (Linux)` feeds the required "All required checks pass" gate, this flake currently blocks every PR. The three PRs above were admin-merged past it after the failure was proven pre-existing on main.

## Evidence from the failing run's trace

Error-context snapshot (run 30063975569, artifact `playwright-test-results-47f0340701366d04b982840ec21b6ecf3ce87b22`) shows:

- `E2E_COMPACTION_HISTORY_ONE` / `_TWO` turns completed with mock replies
- The `E2E_TRIGGER_AUTOMATIC_COMPACTION` message rendered **with its normal mock reply**
- No "Summarizing thread" status ever appeared, and the mock's `holdFirstCompletionContaining('You are a summarization agent...')` hook never captured a summary request

i.e. the failure is at `await fixture.mock.waitForHeldCompletion()` (spec line 130): **automatic compaction never started** within 90s. The queueing logic under test is never reached.

## Where to look

- The spec configures a tiny `threshold_tokens: 22000` budget and expects the 500-repeat trigger message to cross it and start compaction promptly. The race is between turn completion, token accounting, and the compaction scheduler kicking off the summary request.
- Introduced with the recent desktop compression E2E work: #69783 (queue prompts during context compaction) and #69580 (session lifecycle E2E coverage).
- Timing-sensitive tests must not assume a quiet runner (repo flake policy); the fix should be event-based (wait for the compaction-scheduled signal, or nudge the scheduler deterministically in the fixture) rather than a larger timeout.

- main: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/30063335713
- PR #70512: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/30063975569 (original + rerun, both red)

items.title: Usage accounting: OpenAI GPT-5.6+ cache writes and Qwen flat cache reads normalize to 0

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: area/usage-cost
labels.description: Token accounting, usage reporting, billing, cost tracking

items.body:
### Summary

`normalize_usage()` in `agent/usage_pricing.py` undercounts cache token usage for two real, distinct response shapes:

1. **OpenAI Responses API (`codex_responses` mode), GPT-5.6+ explicit cache writes.** The `codex_responses` branch reads `input_tokens_details.cache_creation_tokens` — a field name that does not appear in OpenAI's documented Responses API schema. The documented field for cache writes (billed at 1.25x input price) is `cache_write_tokens`. Any GPT-5.6+ session that actually writes to the explicit cache (see #70382/#70383) reports `cache_write_tokens=0` in Hermes's own accounting, even though OpenAI billed for the write.
2. **Some Alibaba/Qwen regional OpenAI-compatible endpoints, cache reads.** These report cache hits as a flat `usage.cached_tokens`, with no `prompt_tokens_details` wrapper at all — not the standard OpenAI nested shape, not Anthropic's top-level `cache_read_input_tokens`, not DeepSeek's `prompt_cache_hit_tokens`. Responses from these endpoints fall through every existing fallback in the `else` (chat_completions) branch and normalize to `cache_read_tokens=0`.

Both are silent undercounts: no error, no crash, just cost/cache-hit-ratio numbers that are wrong for these two provider shapes.

### Where I looked

- `agent/usage_pricing.py`, `normalize_usage()`, `codex_responses` branch (~line 1134) and the generic OpenAI-compatible `else` branch (~line 1163) — the latter already has DeepSeek (`prompt_cache_hit_tokens`) and Anthropic-style top-level (`cache_read_input_tokens`) fallbacks for cache reads, but nothing for a flat `cached_tokens` and nothing analogous for `codex_responses`-mode cache writes.
- OpenAI's Responses API prompt-caching docs (`input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens`) confirm the correct field name for (1).

### Requested behavior

- `codex_responses` mode: read `input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` first; keep `cache_creation_tokens` as a fallback for any older/alternate Responses-compatible endpoint that still uses that name, rather than dropping it.
- Generic OpenAI-compatible mode: after the existing DeepSeek/Anthropic-style fallbacks, also fall back to a flat top-level `usage.cached_tokens` when nothing else matched.

Ref: internal cache/performance audit (`relatorio-cache-performance-provedores-ia.md`, P1 item 7).

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Describe the bug

The Telegram platform adapter enters a retry-1/5 infinite loop where two `getUpdates` calls are issued nearly simultaneously (~150ms apart), causing a 409 Conflict self-collision.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start Hermes gateway with Telegram platform enabled
2. Observe logs at startup

## Expected behavior
Telegram polling connects cleanly without self-conflict

## Actual behavior
```
[Telegram] Connected to Telegram (polling mode)
[Telegram] set_my_commands OK
[Telegram] Telegram polling conflict (1/5) -- 409 Conflict  <-- 2x within 200ms
[Telegram] Telegram polling resumed after conflict retry 1/5
[Telegram] Telegram polling conflict (1/5)  <-- immediately again
... (infinite loop, never escalates to 2/5)
```

The `_handle_polling_conflict` counter resets to 0 on every successful `start_polling()`, but a second concurrent `getUpdates` call immediately triggers another 409, restarting the 1/5 cycle forever.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v2026.7.7.2
- Docker deployment (WebUI + Agent containers sharing /opt/data)
- Python 3.12
- bot_token valid (sendMessage/getMe work fine via direct API)

## Workaround attempted
- Tried adding `_conflict_recovery_running` guard flag
- Tried adjusting `read_timeout`/`pool_timeout` env vars -- no effect
